video.title: Don't Become A Content Creator, Build A Content Business.

summary: Codie Sanchez explains how to build a content business by choosing one platform, making native and useful content, studying audience response, and turning attention into owned relationships and paid offers. She compares X, TikTok, LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, and newsletters, including claimed sponsorship rates and event-ticket results. Her proposed funnel runs from free content and a newsletter to guides, courses, events, advisory programs, business sourcing, and investments. The main takeaway is to use content to build trust and sell useful offers, rather than relying only on platform ads or sponsorships.

speakers.name: Codie Sanchez
speakers.description: Presents the content strategy and describes her own audience, products, and campaign results.

ideas.name: Content-led business and audience funnel
ideas.one_liner: Use useful content to attract an audience, capture the relationship through a newsletter, and sell progressively deeper products and services.
ideas.business_model: Content-led sales funnel combining sponsorships and platform revenue with owned products, services, events, and investments.
ideas.customer: People interested in buying and growing small businesses, business education, and the topics the creator has earned the right to explain.
ideas.problem: Audiences need useful, credible information; the creator needs a way to turn attention into lasting customer relationships and sales.
ideas.offer: Free content and a newsletter, followed by guides, templates, books, courses, community or events, cohort or membership offers, personalized services, and potentially investment opportunities.

pricing.model: Free content leading to progressively higher-priced offers; sponsorship and platform revenue are additional income streams.

price_points.label: Playbook, course, low-level product, community, or event
Access and speed, such as a cohort or year-long membership
Above this rung: personalized or big-ticket offers

pricing.notes: These are the speaker's general product-ladder ranges, not stated prices for her individual products. She recommends starting with free content, a newsletter, and one paid step.

acquisition_channels.details: Publish platform-native content that teaches or entertains; focus on one platform before expanding.

quote.text: You win on the internet by not being everywhere. You win by being undeniable in one place.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

acquisition_channels.details: Use long-form and short-form videos, case studies, frameworks, and community posts to reach viewers and sell events or offers.

quote.text: One of the most underused features on any platform right now is YouTube community posts.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

acquisition_channels.details: Capture the audience in a newsletter, then use it to sell products and events.

quote.text: So it's the channel you sell the most through. We sold 30% of our tickets through newsletter.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

acquisition_channels.details: Follow high-level employees at platforms and learn from their public posts about what those platforms are looking for.

quote.text: Follow high-level employees working for the platform you're trying to grow on, or active on social.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

ideas.delivery: Publish educational or entertaining content, collect interested viewers through a newsletter, and deliver products or services at different depths. The speaker describes a team reviewing scripts and operating products, but does not specify the full delivery process.
unit_economics_claims: The speaker says organic content accounted for 62% of ticket sales in one campaign, while paid advertising accounted for 38%.
The speaker gives general product-ladder price bands from free through more than $5,000.
The speaker says her newsletter generated 30% of ticket sales for one event.

acquisition.how: Agents could research topics, draft platform-specific content, and report on performance; a person should check expertise, accuracy, and platform fit.

onboarding.how: Following, subscribing, and downloading a self-serve guide can be automated; personalized or high-ticket offers need review.

delivery.how: Digital products can be delivered automatically, but the content, advisory, events, sourcing, and investment work described still needs substantial human input.

billing.how: Payments for digital products and subscriptions can be automated; sponsorships, events, and bespoke services need oversight.

support.how: Agents can answer routine product questions, but audience engagement and personalized advice need human judgment.

uk_applicability.notes: The content, newsletter, and digital-product model works in the UK. For UK acquisition, keep activity inbound or obtain consent before marketing to individuals and sole traders; cold email rules differ for limited companies.

risks: Relying only on platform advertising or brand deals leaves revenue dependent on platform rules and reach.
The funnel may require considerable human expertise, content production, and service delivery before it becomes repeatable.
For UK execution, automated unsolicited marketing by email, text, WhatsApp, or direct message can breach PECR rules for individuals and sole traders.

quotes.text: You build a ladder that solves people's problems at different depths.
quotes.speaker: Codie Sanchez

quotes.text: Do not rely solely on platform ad revenue. Too many people make content and do brand deals and think that's it.
quotes.speaker: Codie Sanchez

quotes.text: You don't build all five on day one. I like starting with free content and adding one paid step
quotes.speaker: Codie Sanchez

ideas.name: X creator and sponsorship channel
ideas.one_liner: Publish fast, opinionated posts and podcast clips on X, with sponsorships as a possible revenue source.
ideas.business_model: Sponsored posts and potential platform payments, supported by organic content.
ideas.customer: X users who like cerebral, challenging, or argumentative posts; sponsors seeking access to that audience.
ideas.problem: Sponsors and creators need attention on a fast-moving platform where content has a short shelf life.
ideas.offer: Predictions, contrarian opinions, and horizontal podcast clips.

pricing.model: Sponsored post; the speaker also says the platform pays creators but gives no separate amount.

price_points.label: At 100,000 followers, approximate range stated by speaker

pricing.notes: The transcript says a couple hundred dollars to a thousand dollars per post.

acquisition_channels.details: Post predictions that invite discussion and use horizontal podcast clips; the speaker says content dies in about a day.

quote.text: Predictions that invite a little fight in the comments. Bad content is feel good aesthetic trying to be liked instead of right.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

ideas.delivery: Create and publish posts or clips; sponsorship delivery is a post. The speaker does not state who handles production or sponsor work.
unit_economics_claims: The speaker estimates $200 to $1,000 per sponsored post at 100,000 followers.
The speaker says just over 1% of tickets for her last event came through X.

acquisition.how: Agents could draft and schedule posts and summarize response; a person should choose the point of view and check the content.

onboarding.how: Followers can arrive and follow without manual onboarding; sponsor qualification and deal terms need review.

delivery.how: Posting and clipping can be assisted by software, but distinctive opinions and sponsor approvals need human input.

billing.how: Invoices and payment reminders can be automated; sponsorship agreements and fulfillment need oversight.

support.how: Agents can triage routine replies, but public discussion and reputation-sensitive responses need human review.

uk_applicability.notes: X and sponsored content can be used in the UK. Keep audience acquisition inbound and disclose commercial relationships appropriately.

risks: The speaker describes a short content shelf life and weak event-ticket contribution from X.
The quoted sponsorship range depends on audience size and is not guaranteed.

quotes.text: If you have 100,000 followers and X sponsorship might be a couple hundred bucks to a thousand per post, that's the lowest of the bunch.
quotes.speaker: Codie Sanchez

ideas.name: TikTok creator and product channel
ideas.one_liner: Use short, stripped-down videos to reach cold audiences, then monetize with sponsorships or visually compelling products.
ideas.business_model: Sponsored posts and product sales, including sales through TikTok Shop.
ideas.customer: TikTok viewers discovering short videos, sponsors, and customers for visually demonstrable products.
ideas.problem: Creators and businesses need awareness among people who do not already follow them; off-platform conversion may be difficult.
ideas.offer: Fast videos with a strong hook, a clear problem, and a quick solution; the speaker says CPG products and books can work well.

price_points.label: At 100,000 followers; range is unclear in the Whisper transcript

pricing.notes: The transcript renders the amount as '2007,000'; interpreted as a $200 to $7,000 range from context. TikTok Shop product prices are not stated.

acquisition_channels.details: Use a strong contrarian hook in the first few seconds, show a problem and solution, and keep production simple.

quote.text: The high performing TikToks get right into it. Like this with a contrarian hook and less than four seconds.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

acquisition_channels.details: TikTok Shop can support product sales; the speaker says visually obvious products and books may fit.

ideas.delivery: Publish short videos and, for product sellers, sell through TikTok Shop or attempt to send buyers off-platform. Product fulfillment is not described.
unit_economics_claims: The speaker estimates $200 to $7,000 per sponsored post at 100,000 followers; the transcript's wording is unclear.
The speaker says a TikTok example received 290,000 views and 441 comments.
The speaker says her account has over 2 million followers and sold fewer than a dozen tickets to her last event.

acquisition.how: Agents can help research trends, draft hooks, and schedule content; a person should supply expertise and approve creative work.

onboarding.how: Following or buying through a shop can be self-serve; customer questions and unusual orders need review.

delivery.how: Video production can be assisted, but creative quality and physical product fulfillment still require human work.

billing.how: Shop payments can be automated; sponsorship billing and refunds need oversight.

support.how: Agents can answer common product questions, but complaints and order exceptions need a person.

uk_applicability.notes: Short-form content and product commerce can work in the UK, subject to local shop availability, product rules, and consumer obligations. The transcript does not discuss UK-specific setup.

risks: The speaker says TikTok is good for awareness but poor for event sales and off-platform conversion.
Physical product fulfillment and customer service limit unattended operation.
The spoken sponsorship range is unclear in the Whisper transcript.

quotes.text: TikTok is great for awareness, terrible for sales, unless you have a really viral product that's very easy to see visually.
quotes.speaker: Codie Sanchez

ideas.name: LinkedIn creator and lead magnet channel

ideas.customer: Professionals and business decision-makers interested in improving their work, hiring, or business results.
ideas.problem: Professionals want useful, credible content; businesses want access to people who influence decisions.
ideas.offer: Tactical education, professional aspiration, frameworks, quotes, and a free hiring matrix as a lead magnet.

pricing.model: Sponsored posts and indirect business value from leads, clients, or hires.

price_points.label: At 100,000 followers, approximate range stated by speaker

pricing.notes: The speaker says LinkedIn itself does not currently pay creators for activity on the platform.

acquisition_channels.details: Share practical professional posts, contrarian frameworks, and lead magnets such as a hiring matrix.

quote.text: The way you win is combining professional aspiration with tactical education.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

ideas.delivery: Publish posts and provide a free hiring matrix; downstream leads may become clients or hires. The speaker does not state a complete fulfillment process.
unit_economics_claims: The speaker estimates $1,500 to $8,000 per sponsored post at 100,000 followers.
The speaker says 2.4% of her event tickets were sold through LinkedIn.

acquisition.how: Agents can draft and assess posts and organize inbound leads; a person should approve professional claims and commercial outreach.

onboarding.how: A lead magnet can be delivered automatically; qualifying advisory or business leads needs human judgment.

delivery.how: Content and downloads can be automated in part, but expertise, hiring advice, and client delivery need human input.

billing.how: Sponsored-post invoices can be automated; custom agreements and client services need oversight.

support.how: Agents can handle routine download questions, but professional or hiring advice should be reviewed by a person.

uk_applicability.notes: LinkedIn is usable for UK professional audiences. Keep marketing outreach compliant with UK rules, particularly when contacting individuals or sole traders.

risks: The speaker says LinkedIn did not drive many ticket sales for her event and does not pay creators directly.
Sponsored-post rates are claims, not guaranteed earnings.
Unsolicited automated direct messages can create UK marketing-compliance risk.

quotes.text: Like 1,500 to 8,000 person sponsored posts on 100k followers. That's before the deals clients' hires it brings in
quotes.speaker: Codie Sanchez

onboarding.how: Followers and event customers can self-serve; sponsorship and event questions may need human handling.

billing.how: Ticket and product checkout can be automated; sponsor agreements and event exceptions need review.

risks: The speaker says organic reach has declined and that lifestyle-focused formats can be difficult for creators who do not want to project that image.
The sponsorship range and reach figures are claims, not guaranteed outcomes.

quotes.text: At 100k followers on Instagram, sponsorships run about 2500 to 75, 100 opposed.

Sponsorship and advertising figures are speaker claims and are not guaranteed.

tactics.name: Choose one platform before expanding
steps: Select one platform where the founder can produce content consistently.
Study what performs there and adapt to that platform's style and audience.
Expand to other platforms after establishing a repeatable approach.

quote.text: Pick one platform, win on it, then expand it.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Build a swipe file and problem bank
steps: Search the niche and filter to videos.
Save the top 100 posts with over a million views.
Record each thumbnail, transcribe its first 30 seconds, note its top comments, and identify sponsors.
Reuse proven hooks while adding original expertise; do not copy the content.
Write scripts before filming, and save audience questions in the audience's own words.

quote.text: Then you screenshot the thumbnail, transcribe the first 30 seconds and log the top comments. And who's sponsoring them? That's your future revenue list.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Use unanswered audience questions for new content
steps: Read comments under popular videos and look for unanswered questions.
Check relevant comment sections, subreddits, and Discords.
Turn a specific unanswered question into the next piece of content.
Keep a problem bank using the audience's own wording.

quote.text: The lazy person copies the video on top, but I think the smart one actually reads the unanswered questions underneath, comment sections, sub-readets, discords.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Review content performance and iterate
steps: For each post, record why people started watching, where they left, and which line got a reaction.
Review winners and flops to identify topic, specificity, and hook patterns.
Use the relevant platform metrics: click-through and watch time on YouTube, shares and watch time on Instagram, replies on X, engagement on LinkedIn, and opens for newsletters.
Use the findings to revise future scripts and formats.

quote.text: After posts, just three notes. Why did they start watching? Where did they leave? What line got a reaction?
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Build credibility without a studio
steps: Make content native to the platform's style, pacing, and editing conventions.
Explain things the creator has actually done and can discuss without preparation.
Show the work in context when possible, such as filming a real project on site.

quote.text: So don't ask, what should I post? Ask, what have I earned the right to explain?
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Start with a small product ladder
steps: Start with free content and a newsletter that captures the relationship.
Add one paid product, such as a guide or template.
Add higher-priced offers only when the offer below is full.

quote.text: I like starting with free content and adding one paid step, a free newsletter that captures the relationship, plus a single low ticket guide as your first wrung
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Make the hook and value arrive early
steps: Open with a counterintuitive hook that promises clear value.
Deliver the promised value quickly and avoid repetition.
Review retention to find where viewers leave and remove slow sections.

quote.text: The hook should be counterintuitive, promise value. You've got to deliver that value right away and don't repeat yourself.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Do not spread effort across many platforms by publishing a large volume of average content; the speaker recommends focusing on one platform first.

quote.text: They spray and prey, pumping out 25 average pieces a week across six platforms, none of which work, and then they wonder why nothing hits.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Overproduced studio content may perform worse than simpler, platform-native content.

quote.text: Across the board, we found the more produced we tried to make content, the worse it performs.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Do not copy another creator's full content; borrow proven hooks and add original expertise.

quote.text: After you've done that, steal the hook, not the content. You don't want to be a copycat.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Do not rely only on ad revenue and brand deals; the speaker says her larger business revenue comes from other products and services.

quote.text: Do not rely solely on platform ad revenue. Too many people make content and do brand deals and think that's it.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: A newsletter with filler can train readers to stop opening.

quote.text: If you have a bad newsletter, it's going to give you filler, and it trains people to stop opening, so don't do that.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: A newsletter promotion that only shows off a product without giving the reader something useful may feel selfish and fail to bridge customer and brand.

quote.text: It doesn't bridge the gap between customer and brand, except to show off the product. It feels a little selfish.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: For UK execution, do not automate unsolicited marketing emails, texts, WhatsApp messages, or direct messages to individuals and sole traders without consent; screen cold calls against TPS or CTPS.

lessons.lesson: Start with one platform and learn its audience and content style before expanding.

quote.text: Pick one platform, win on it, then expand it.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Make content native to the platform instead of imposing one production style everywhere.

quote.text: Every platform has its own font, pacing, kind of editing, feel.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Build credibility from experience the creator can explain or show, rather than relying on a polished set.

quote.text: So don't ask, what should I post? Ask, what have I earned the right to explain?
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Use audience questions and wording to generate relevant content instead of inventing topics in isolation.

quote.text: Use the listener's version. Speak it back and they think you read their mind.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Treat performance data as feedback about audience interest, not as a judgment of personal worth.

quote.text: And remember, the data isn't a judgment of your worth. It's a map.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Review the hook, retention, and audience response so successful content can be repeated deliberately.

quote.text: If you can't name it, you can't repeat it. And luck is like a very stupid strategy.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: A large audience is not enough; platform reach and purchase behavior differ, so track the business result that matters.

quote.text: TikTok is great for awareness, terrible for sales, unless you have a really viral product that's very easy to see visually.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Build a route from free value to offers that solve progressively deeper customer problems.

quote.text: You build a ladder that solves people's problems at different depths.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: A smaller, engaged newsletter audience may be more valuable to sponsors and sales than a larger inactive list.

quote.text: Which means it's better to have like a small loyal list than a big checked out one.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Ship a useful version before perfection; adding the final polish can take time without being noticed by the audience.

quote.text: Shipped before you feel it's perfect, a 85% in the last 15% takes weeks, and no one notices it for you.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

evidence_quality.rationale: The speaker describes her own content funnel, audience, platform results, ticket attribution, and examples from her videos. Many benchmark figures are broad claims without source details, and the local Whisper transcript contains apparent recognition errors in several prices, names, and phrases.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The speaker promotes her newsletter, a content log used by her team, and her own books, academy, boardroom, Private Client programs, events, and investment activity.
